feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 7 (y 0.05 m, mass 0.5 kg, track 0.10 m, body 0.10 m) is the best raced design at 315.3, with oval finish 75%, s-bend progress 0.140 and slalom progress 0.186. Iteration 8 (same design with y 0.03 m) fell to 209.2, with oval finish 40% and slalom progress 0.075. So sensor lead should stay at 0.05 m. Iteration 6 (mass 0.6 kg, same otherwise) gave oval finish 65% and s-bend and slalom progress 0.181 and 0.191. The s-bend and slalom still end at max_error about 0.062 to 0.064 on every design, so the limit is not sensing lead or mass alone. Decide the next change from the race. If the oval finish rate drops below 65% with y 0.05 m, mass 0.5 kg is not helping and mass 0.6 kg is the known-stable setting. If s-bend and slalom max_error stays at about 0.062 with progress below 0.2, the sensing footprint and spacing are the next thing to test. body_width cannot help because the off-track limit is already at its floor.
requested_changes: If the oval finish rate falls below 65% at y 0.05 m, set mass back to 0.6 kg and keep the 0.10 m track and 0.10 m body. Evidence: iteration 6 at mass 0.6 kg gave a 65% oval finish, while iteration 7 at mass 0.5 kg gave 75%, so the lower mass helps the oval but its direction is not yet clear on the bends.

If s-bend and slalom max_error stays at about 0.062 with progress below 0.2 at y 0.05 m, try a 7-sensor array at x = -0.08 to 0.08 with 0.027 m spacing, keeping sensor_size 0.016 and y 0.05 m. Evidence: iteration 8 showed the lead is not the limit, and iterations 3 to 7 with 0.04 m spacing still ended off_track at max_error 0.062, so finer spacing may improve the centre-line signal.

If the oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25 at mass 0.5 kg, keep the geometry and set kd to 0.8 in the controller. Evidence: oval oscillation was 0.267 in iteration 2 and 0.275 in iteration 1, both above the threshold, while iteration 7 was 0.208, so this is a headroom check only.
